title: Pointwise differential criterion for smoothness
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], let $x\in X$, let $s=f(x)$, and put $d=\dim_x(X_s)$ for the dimension at $x$ [def-kun-dimension] of the fibre $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Say that $f$ is smooth at $x$ if there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that $f|_U:U\to S$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Then $f$ is smooth at $x$ if and only if the local ring map $\mathcal O_{S,s}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and the $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module $\Omega^1_{X/S,x}$, the stalk of the relative differential sheaf [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], can be generated by at most $d$ elements.

source.place: Tag 01V9 (morphisms-lemma-smooth-at-point), equivalence of (1) and (3); 'smooth at x' as in Morphisms Definition 01V5

proof.text: Suppose first that $f$ is smooth on an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$. By [lem-pc-smooth-flat] and [def-weil-flat-morphism], its stalk map at $x$ is flat. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-differentials-free-rank-fibre-dimension] to $U\to S$. The fibre $U_s$ is the open subspace of $X_s$ above $U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], so [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace] identifies its dimension at $x$ with $d$. The cited rank lemma gives affine neighbourhoods $W\subset U$, $V\subset S$ on which $\Omega_{A/R}$ is free of rank $d$, where $A=\mathcal O_X(W)$ and $R=\mathcal O_S(V)$. By [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] its associated sheaf is $\Omega^1_{X/S}|_W$, and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization] identifies its stalk with $(\Omega_{A/R})_{\mathfrak q}$. Localizing a basis gives a generating family of $d$ elements: a fraction $\sum_i a_i e_i/t$ equals $\sum_i(a_i/t)(e_i/1)$. This proves the forward implication.

source.place: Tag 01V9 (lemma-smooth-at-point), (1) implies (3); Tags 01VF and 02G1; Schemes Tag 01HV(7)

proof.text: For the converse, assume the flatness and generator bound of the statement. By [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] choose affine neighbourhoods $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $x$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $s$ such that $f(W)\subset V$ and $A$ is finitely presented over $R$. Let $\varphi:R\to A$ be the induced map, and let $\mathfrak q$ represent $x$. The commutative square of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-induced-ring-map-spec-square] shows that $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ represents $s$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-stalk-localization] the stalk map is $R_{\mathfrak p}\to A_{\mathfrak q}$; thus this local map is flat. Set $M=\Omega_{A/R}$. By [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization], $M_{\mathfrak q}\cong\Omega^1_{X/S,x}$ over $A_{\mathfrak q}\cong\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Hence $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is generated by $r\le d$ elements.

source.place: Tag 01V9, proof of (3) implies (2), affine reduction; Definition 01TP; Schemes Tags 01HV and 01I1

proof.text: Put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $F=k\otimes_R A$. The affine stalk identifications [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification] identify $k$ with $\kappa(s)$ compatibly with the canonical morphism to $S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $\operatorname{Spec}F\cong W\times_V\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the open subscheme of $X_s$ above $W$ (interchanging tensor factors by $a\otimes\lambda\leftrightarrow\lambda\otimes a$). Let $\mathfrak Q$ be the point above $x$. Its contraction to $A$ is $\mathfrak q$, since the first projection is induced by $a\mapsto1\otimes a$. Equivalently, $\mathfrak Q$ is the kernel of $F\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, $\lambda\otimes a\mapsto\lambda\bar a$: that kernel contracts to $\mathfrak q$ and the fibre has a unique point above $x$ by [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace] we have $\dim_{\mathfrak Q}(\operatorname{Spec}F)=d$; the isomorphism preserves this dimension because it bijects open neighbourhoods and chains of irreducible closed subsets. If $A=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(h_1,\ldots,h_m)$, then $F=k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_m)$ by the tensor-product universal property. Thus $F$ is a finite type $k$-algebra, and [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] gives finite dimension of $\operatorname{Spec}F$. Its dimension at $\mathfrak Q$ is finite and nonnegative, since it is bounded by the dimension of the whole space and every neighbourhood contains $\mathfrak Q$.

source.place: Tag 01V9, proof reducing (3) to the fibre; Schemes Tags 01JQ and 01JR; Topology Tag 0055; Algebra Tag 00TT

proof.text:
Let $L=\kappa(\mathfrak Q)$. Because $\mathfrak Q$ contracts to $\mathfrak q$, every $a\in A\setminus\mathfrak q$ maps to a nonzero element of $L$; hence $A\to L$ extends to $A_{\mathfrak q}\to L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change] there is an $F$-linear isomorphism $\Omega_{F/k}\cong F\otimes_A M$. Tensoring with $L$ gives
$$\Omega_{F/k}\otimes_F L\cong M_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak q}}L.$$
Explicitly, on the right-to-left map, $(\omega/a)\otimes\lambda$ goes to $(1\otimes\omega)\otimes(\lambda/\bar a)$ after using the base-change isomorphism. The inverse sends $(b\otimes\omega)\otimes\lambda$ to $(\omega/1)\otimes\bar b\lambda$. The tensor balancing and localization relations make these inverse maps. If $m_1,\ldots,m_r$ generate $M_{\mathfrak q}$, then $m_i\otimes1$ span its tensor with $L$: expand $m\otimes\lambda=\sum_i m_i\otimes a_i\lambda$ whenever $m=\sum_i a_i m_i$. Therefore
$$\dim_L(\Omega_{F/k}\otimes_F L)\le r\le d=\dim_{\mathfrak Q}(\operatorname{Spec}F).$$

source.place: Tag 00RV (lemma-differentials-base-change); used in Morphisms Tag 01V9, proof of (3) implies (2)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-differentials-dimension-bound-smooth-at-prime] to the field $k$, its finite type algebra $F$, and $\mathfrak Q$, with the inequality of step 4. It gives that $k\to F$ is smooth at $\mathfrak Q$. Now apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-smooth-fibre-smooth-at-prime] to $R\to A$, $\mathfrak p$, $\mathfrak q$. Its finite-presentation hypothesis holds with $g=1$; its local flatness is step 2; its fibre is $A\otimes_R k$, identified with $F$ by tensor commutation, with the same prime above $\mathfrak q$. Consequently $R\to A$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q$. By [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal], there exists $g\in A\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $R\to A_g$ is a smooth ring map.

source.place: Tag 01V9, (3) implies (2) by Algebra Tag 00TT and (2) implies (1) by Algebra Tag 00TF; Algebra Definition 00TB

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], $\operatorname{Spec}A_g$ identifies with an open neighbourhood $W_g=D(g)$ of $x$ in $W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], the restriction $h:W_g\to V$ is smooth. It is also smooth as a morphism to $S$: its affine finite-presentation neighbourhoods over $V$ are still such neighbourhoods over $S$, by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. For formal smoothness, take any first order thickening $T\subset T'$ of affine $S$-schemes and $T\to W_g$ over $S$. By [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], $T$ and $T'$ have the same underlying points. Since the given $T\to S$ lands in the open $V$, so does $T'\to S$, which therefore factors uniquely through the open subscheme $V$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. The square is now over $V$, so formal smoothness of $h$ lifts it to $T'\to W_g$ by [def-sbc-formally-smooth]. This is also a lift over $S$. Thus $W_g\to S$ is locally of finite presentation and formally smooth, hence smooth by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. As $x\in W_g$, $f$ is smooth at $x$, proving the converse.
